title: Renal Function Tests: BUN, Creatinine, eGFR and Electrolytes
summary: Markers of glomerular filtration, the BUN/creatinine ratio and interpretation of sodium and potassium disturbances.
objectives: Interpret BUN and creatinine together using the BUN/creatinine ratio.

highYield: Creatinine is a more specific marker of GFR than BUN (BUN is affected by diet, hydration and liver function).
BUN/creatinine ratio > 20:1 suggests prerenal azotemia or GI bleed; < 10:1 suggests liver disease or rhabdomyolysis.
Pseudohyperkalemia: hemolyzed sample, prolonged tourniquet use, or marked thrombocytosis/leukocytosis.

deepStudy.introduction: Renal function is assessed primarily by estimating glomerular filtration. Creatinine-based equations (CKD-EPI) account for age and sex; reference intervals vary by method and population.

sections.heading: Urea vs creatinine
sections.body: Urea (BUN) is produced by the liver, reabsorbed in the tubules and influenced by protein intake and catabolism. Creatinine comes from muscle creatine phosphate, is freely filtered and partially secreted; it is relatively stable but method-dependent (Jaffe vs enzymatic).

sections.heading: Sodium and potassium
sections.body: True hyponatremia is usually dilutional (high ADH states). Potassium must be interpreted with hemolysis checks — a single hemolyzed sample is the most common cause of spurious potassium elevation in the lab.

deepStudy.clinicalSignificance: Early detection of reduced eGFR allows intervention that slows progression to end-stage renal disease.
deepStudy.labInterpretation: Never report a potassium value from a visibly hemolyzed sample without a comment or recollection; verify reference intervals per local laboratory.
examTraps: BUN rises with GI bleeding (protein digestion) — do not automatically attribute a high BUN/creatinine ratio to dehydration.
eGFR equations are not valid in acute kidney injury (non-steady-state creatinine).

memoryHooks.text: BUN = Blame Urine Nitrogen if ratio > 20: think prerenal.
memoryHooks.funny: Bantay: 'Pag sobrang taas ng BUN: prerenal daw — or kumain ka lang ng maraming lechon.'

references.title: Tietz Textbook of Clinical Chemistry and Molecular Diagnostics

reviewerNote: Reference intervals vary by laboratory, method, age, sex and population; verify against your local laboratory.
